newsitem.title: FRANCE: Juppe says not campaigning to keep job as premier.
newsitem.headline: Juppe says not campaigning to keep job as premier.

text.p: French Prime Minister Alain Juppe said on Sunday it was up to President Jacques Chirac to name the premier if his centre-right coalition wins a snap parliamentary election and insisted he was not campaigning to keep the job.

"I'm absolutely not a candidate for my own succession," Juppe told TF1 television ahead of the May 25-June 1 vote. "It would be very arrogant and insolent to say 'it's me'. It's absurd. It is the president who decides."

Opinion polls in late 1996 showed that Juppe, 51, was the least popular prime minister in the Fifth Republic, blamed for record unemployment and austerity to help France qualify for a single European currency. The Socialist and Communist opposition has made him their central target.
"My only ambition is to help to win this campaign because I believe it is in the interest of France" for the centre-right coalition to keep its National Assembly majority, he said.

He said Chirac could chose a prime minister from a wide number of politicians on the right. "What I've done in the past two years has not been easy. There were moments of great tension, it's taken courage...And the results show progress," he said.

If re-elected, the coalition would seek to implement a series of new measures within 40 days, setting a five-year plan for expenditure and revenue to ensure that public spending did not increase in real terms, Juppe said.
